Risk Title: Chatbot hallucinations give clients wrong guidance
Controls / Mitigation: Retrieval-augmented generation limited to an approved knowledge base; confidence threshold with handoff to a human consultant; weekly sampled output review; on-screen AI disclaimer
Key Risk Indicator (KRI): Hallucination rate above 2% in the weekly 200-response sample
Framework Mapping: NIST AI RMF MEASURE 2.5; ISO/IEC 42001 Annex A.6; EU AI Act Art. 50
Description (Cause -> Event -> Consequen: Cause: the LLM produces plausible but unsupported answers. Event: TA-Assist gives a client incorrect technical or compliance guidance. Consequence: the client acts on bad advice, leading to a contract dispute and reputational harm.

Risk Title: Prompt injection exposes internal data through the chatbot
Controls / Mitigation: Input and output filtering; system prompt isolation; least-privilege access for connected tools; quarterly AI red-team exercise; prompt and response logging to the SIEM
Key Risk Indicator (KRI): Any successful red-team bypass; blocked injection attempts per week trending up
Framework Mapping: NIST AI RMF MEASURE 2.7; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Apps (LLM01); EU AI Act Art. 15
Description (Cause -> Event -> Consequen: Cause: malicious instructions hidden in user input or retrieved documents. Event: the chatbot ignores its guardrails and reveals internal or other clients' data. Consequence: data breach, breach-notification duties, loss of client trust.

Controls / Mitigation: Annual independent bias audit; adverse impact ratio monitoring by demographic group; human review of every automated rejection; candidate notice and alternative process
Key Risk Indicator (KRI): Adverse impact ratio below 0.80 (four-fifths rule) for any group
Framework Mapping: NIST AI RMF MEASURE 2.11; EU AI Act Annex III (employment, high-risk); NYC Local Law 144
Description (Cause -> Event -> Consequen: Cause: historical hiring data reflects past bias. Event: TalentMatch ranks qualified candidates from protected groups lower. Consequence: discriminatory hiring outcomes, legal claims and regulatory penalties.

Risk Title: Staff paste confidential client data into public AI tools
Controls / Mitigation: Acceptable AI use policy; approved enterprise AI tools only; DLP rules blocking uploads to unapproved AI sites; mandatory staff training
Key Risk Indicator (KRI): DLP alerts for AI sites per month; share of staff who completed AI use training
Framework Mapping: NIST AI RMF GOVERN 1.1; ISO/IEC 42001 Annex A.2 and A.7; GDPR Art. 5 and 32
Description (Cause -> Event -> Consequen: Cause: no approved AI tool and no clear policy. Event: consultants paste client contracts or personal data into free public chatbots. Consequence: confidentiality breach, contract violations and privacy fines.

Risk Title: Model drift degrades client risk scores
Controls / Mitigation: Monthly drift monitoring (Population Stability Index); automatic retraining trigger; champion-challenger validation before release; model card updated each release
Key Risk Indicator (KRI): PSI above 0.25 on key features; AUC drops more than 5 points
Framework Mapping: NIST AI RMF MEASURE 2.4 and MANAGE 4.1; ISO/IEC 42001 Annex A.6
Description (Cause -> Event -> Consequen: Cause: client portfolios and market conditions change after training. Event: RiskLens scores become less accurate over time. Consequence: clients make poor risk decisions based on stale scores.

Risk Title: Dependence on a single third-party LLM provider
Controls / Mitigation: Contract SLA with service credits; vendor AI risk assessment before renewal; abstraction layer allowing a fallback model; documented exit plan
Key Risk Indicator (KRI): Provider uptime below 99.5% in a month; unannounced model version changes
Framework Mapping: NIST AI RMF GOVERN 6.1 and MANAGE 3.1; ISO/IEC 42001 Annex A.10
Description (Cause -> Event -> Consequen: Cause: both products call one external LLM API. Event: the provider has an outage, raises prices or changes model behavior. Consequence: service interruption, SLA breaches with clients and unplanned costs.

Risk Title: Training data poisoning in the forecasting pipeline
Controls / Mitigation: Data provenance checks; signed data sources; anomaly detection on training sets; restricted write access to the feature store
Key Risk Indicator (KRI): Unexplained shifts in input data distributions; unauthorized writes to the feature store
Framework Mapping: NIST AI RMF MEASURE 2.7; ISO/IEC 42001 Annex A.7; EU AI Act Art. 10 and 15
Description (Cause -> Event -> Consequen: Cause: weak controls over third-party data feeds. Event: an attacker injects manipulated records into training data. Consequence: skewed forecasts that cost clients inventory and revenue.

Risk Title: Clients cannot get clear explanations of risk scores
Controls / Mitigation: SHAP-based reason codes for each score; client-facing model documentation; plain-language explanation template for account managers
Key Risk Indicator (KRI): Explanation requests not answered within 10 business days
Framework Mapping: NIST AI RMF MEASURE 2.9; EU AI Act Art. 13; GDPR Art. 22
Description (Cause -> Event -> Consequen: Cause: a complex ensemble model with no built-in explanations. Event: a client or regulator asks why an entity received a high score and we cannot answer clearly. Consequence: lost renewals and regulatory findings.

Risk Title: Non-compliance with EU AI Act obligations for EU clients
Controls / Mitigation: Classify each AI system against EU AI Act risk tiers; gap assessment; technical documentation for high-risk systems; legal review of EU client contracts
Key Risk Indicator (KRI): High-risk systems without a completed gap assessment
Framework Mapping: EU AI Act Art. 9, 11 and 17; ISO/IEC 42001 clause 6.1; NIST AI RMF GOVERN 1.1
Description (Cause -> Event -> Consequen: Cause: EU obligations are new and still being phased in. Event: a system used by EU clients is found to lack required documentation or oversight. Consequence: fines, forced withdrawal from the EU market and client churn.

Controls / Mitigation: Human review before anything is published; vendor IP indemnity clause; rule against reproducing copyrighted sources in client deliverables
Key Risk Indicator (KRI): IP complaints or takedown requests received
Framework Mapping: NIST AI RMF MAP 4.1; ISO/IEC 42001 Annex A.10
Description (Cause -> Event -> Consequen: Cause: generative models can reproduce protected text or images. Event: a deliverable or marketing asset contains infringing material. Consequence: legal claims, takedowns and reputational damage.

Controls / Mitigation: Mandatory peer review of AI-assisted code; SAST and dependency scanning in the CI pipeline; secret scanning; secure coding training
Key Risk Indicator (KRI): High or critical SAST findings per release
Framework Mapping: NIST SP 800-218 (SSDF); OWASP Top 10 for LLM Apps; ISO/IEC 42001 Annex A.9
Description (Cause -> Event -> Consequen: Cause: developers accept AI code suggestions without enough review. Event: vulnerable code or hard-coded secrets ship to production. Consequence: exploitable vulnerabilities in client-facing systems.

Risk Title: Consultants over-rely on AI outputs (automation bias)
Controls / Mitigation: Human-in-the-loop sign-off on client deliverables; AI output review checklist; quarterly spot audits of deliverables
Key Risk Indicator (KRI): Deliverables issued without documented human review
Framework Mapping: NIST AI RMF GOVERN 3.2; EU AI Act Art. 14; ISO/IEC 42001 Annex A.9
Description (Cause -> Event -> Consequen: Cause: time pressure and trust in AI tools. Event: consultants pass AI output to clients without checking it. Consequence: errors in client work and professional liability exposure.

Risk Title: Incomplete inventory of AI systems in use
Controls / Mitigation: Central AI system inventory; intake form for new AI use cases; quarterly attestation from department heads; SaaS discovery tooling
Key Risk Indicator (KRI): AI tools discovered that are not in the inventory
Framework Mapping: NIST AI RMF GOVERN 1.6; ISO/IEC 42001 Annex A.4 and A.6
Description (Cause -> Event -> Consequen: Cause: teams adopt AI features in SaaS tools without telling IT. Event: AI systems run with no owner, risk assessment or monitoring. Consequence: unmanaged risk that this register cannot see.

Controls / Mitigation: Encrypted model storage; role-based access with MFA; access logging and alerting; rate limits on the scoring API to deter model extraction
Key Risk Indicator (KRI): Unusual API query volume; failed access attempts on the model registry
Framework Mapping: NIST AI RMF MEASURE 2.7; ISO/IEC 27001 Annex A.8; EU AI Act Art. 15
Description (Cause -> Event -> Consequen: Cause: model files and the scoring API are attractive targets. Event: an insider or attacker copies or extracts the model. Consequence: loss of competitive advantage and possible misuse of the model.

Risk Title: Staff lack AI literacy for safe use
Controls / Mitigation: Role-based AI literacy training; annual refresher; completion tracked in the learning management system
Framework Mapping: EU AI Act Art. 4; NIST AI RMF GOVERN 2.2; ISO/IEC 42001 clause 7.2
Description (Cause -> Event -> Consequen: Cause: rapid AI adoption without training. Event: staff misuse tools or miss warning signs. Consequence: errors, data leaks and failure to meet AI literacy expectations.

Risk Title: Chat logs keep personal data longer than policy allows
Controls / Mitigation: 30-day log retention with automated deletion; PII redaction before storage; data protection impact assessment (DPIA) completed
Key Risk Indicator (KRI): Records older than 30 days found in the log store
Framework Mapping: GDPR Art. 5(1)(e) and 35; NIST AI RMF MEASURE 2.10; ISO/IEC 42001 Annex A.7
Description (Cause -> Event -> Consequen: Cause: conversation logs are kept indefinitely for model tuning. Event: personal data is held past its retention period. Consequence: privacy violations and a larger impact if logs are breached.

Risk Title: Fallback model gives lower-quality answers during outages
Controls / Mitigation: Risk formally accepted by the AI Governance Committee; status banner tells users when the fallback model is active
Key Risk Indicator (KRI): Hours per month on the fallback model
Description (Cause -> Event -> Consequen: Cause: the backup model is smaller and less capable. Event: during a primary provider outage, answers are shorter or less accurate. Consequence: minor client inconvenience; cost of a premium backup outweighs the benefit.
